# Paths the full deploy leaves alone on the server.
#
# The exclude list governs deletion as well as upload, so anything named here is
# not merely skipped: it is invisible to the sync, and the server's copy is left
# exactly as it is rather than being treated as something deleted locally.
#
# Lines beginning with # are stripped by the workflow before the list is handed
# to the FTP action, which would otherwise take them for glob patterns.

# Repository plumbing and tooling; none of it is part of the site.
**/.git*
**/.git*/**
**/node_modules/**
**/tools/**
**/*.md
_proto/**

# The two files the `config-only` scope ships. They are excluded here so that
# exactly one scope owns them, which is what makes the staged first deploy work:
# web.config carries the 747-entry redirect map, and those redirects point at
# pages that only exist once a content deploy has run. Content therefore has to
# land first, and it can only land first if the full scope leaves web.config
# alone. It also keeps the rollback honest - if the config has to be pulled off
# the server, a later content deploy will not quietly put it back.
web.config
404.htm

# Photographs. ~5.3 GB of originals live only on the server and are uploaded by
# hand. Excluding them is what keeps a deploy from treating the archive as
# something deleted locally.
**/*.jpg
**/*.jpeg

# ...but a file pattern only protects a file the sync actually considers, and
# that is not the whole story. The sync also prunes any *directory* that is on
# the server and not in the checkout, recursively, without consulting the list
# above -- there is no file to match against, only a folder to remove.
#
# That is not hypothetical. Retiring the 8,036 per-photo pages emptied every
# you/**/page-N/ and you/**/gallery/ folder of tracked files. On the runner they
# then did not exist at all, so the first full deploy removed them from the
# server and took 16,479 photographs with them. /galleries/ came through
# untouched only because its folders still hold a tracked index.htm.
#
# Naming the directories keeps the sync out of them entirely. They hold nothing
# but photographs now that the pages are retired, so there is nothing in them a
# deploy should ever manage.
you/**/gallery/**
you/**/page-*/**

# The same trap, found by audit rather than by damage: these folders hold
# photographs and contain no tracked file either, so the checkout has no such
# directory and a deploy would prune them exactly as it pruned the two above.
# They survived only because they are not under you/. Excluding them costs
# nothing, since nothing tracked lives in any of them.
galleries/store/**
galleries/navigation/**
galleries/2017/09/morrisdayandthetime/**
tearsheets/images/**
festivals/2016/**

# Superseded duplicate of you/2023. Nothing links into it and it is not in the
# sitemap, so shipping its 1,788 files would only spend 148 MB of the App
# Service quota on unreachable copies.
you/2023/Old/**

# Build inputs and page templates. web.config answers 404 for these paths, so
# there is no reason for them to occupy the server at all. They used to be
# listed in robots.txt, which published their names to anyone who asked.
you/!template/**
tearsheets/!template.htm
galleries/0000/**
catalog/*/_data/**
galleries/2012/06/test/**
galleries/2016/06/test/**
galleries/2016/06/test2/**
